prompt.adult: In Jesus' story of the hurt traveler, who had compassion and helped him?
prompt.child: In Jesus' story, a man was hurt on the road. Who felt sorry for him and stopped to help?
prompt.teen: In Jesus' story about the hurt traveler, who showed compassion on him?
prompt.older: In the parable recorded in Luke 10:33, who had compassion on the wounded traveler?

verses.text: But a certain Samaritan, as he journeyed, came where he was. And when he saw him, he had compassion.

explanation.adult: Luke 10:33 names the man who had compassion. Read the start of the verse.
explanation.child: Read Luke 10:33. The verse tells who came along and felt sorry for the hurt man.
explanation.teen: Check Luke 10:33. It names the traveler who had compassion.
explanation.older: Luke 10:33 identifies the one who had compassion at the opening of the verse.

teaching.extended_explanation: Two men passed by on the other side. Luke 10:33 introduces the third man, the one who stopped and cared.
teaching.takeaway: A Samaritan had compassion and helped the hurt man.

prompt.adult: In the story, what did the helper pour on the hurt man's wounds?
prompt.child: The helper in Jesus' story bandaged the hurt man. What did he pour on the wounds?
prompt.teen: What did the helper in the story pour on the hurt man's wounds?
prompt.older: According to Luke 10:34, what did the helper pour on the wounded man's injuries?

verses.text: So he went to him and bandaged his wounds, pouring on oil and wine; and he set him on his own animal, brought him to an inn, and took care of him.

explanation.adult: Luke 10:34 tells how the helper cared for the wounds. Read the words after "pouring on."
explanation.child: Read Luke 10:34. Find "pouring on." The next words tell what he used.
explanation.teen: Check Luke 10:34. What he poured is named right after "pouring on."
explanation.older: Luke 10:34 names what was poured on the wounds, right after the word "pouring."

teaching.extended_explanation: Luke 10:34 lists the helper's care step by step: he bandaged, poured something on, set the man on his animal, and took him to an inn.
teaching.takeaway: The helper poured oil and wine on the man's wounds.

prompt.adult: In Jesus' story of the lost sheep, how many sheep did the man have in all?
prompt.child: In Jesus' story, a man lost one of his sheep. How many sheep did he have to start with?
prompt.teen: In the story of the lost sheep, how many sheep did the man have altogether?
prompt.older: In the parable in Luke 15:4, how many sheep did the man have in all?

verses.text: “What man of you, having a hundred sheep, if he loses one of them, does not leave the ninety-nine in the wilderness, and go after the one which is lost until he finds it?

explanation.adult: Luke 15:4 gives the total number of sheep near the start of the verse.
explanation.child: Read Luke 15:4. The total number of sheep comes before he loses one.
explanation.teen: Check Luke 15:4. The total is given before the verse says one was lost.
explanation.older: Luke 15:4 states the size of the flock before describing the one that was lost.

teaching.extended_explanation: Luke 15:4 gives two numbers: the whole flock and the number left behind. The whole flock is named first.
teaching.takeaway: The man in the story had a hundred sheep.

prompt.adult: Jesus said there will be more of what in heaven over one sinner who repents?
prompt.child: Jesus said heaven has more of something when one person turns back to God. What is it?
prompt.teen: When one sinner repents, Jesus said heaven has more of what?
prompt.older: According to Luke 15:7, what will there be more of in heaven over one sinner who repents?

verses.text: I say to you that likewise there will be more joy in heaven over one sinner who repents than over ninety-nine just persons who need no repentance.

explanation.adult: Luke 15:7 tells what heaven has more of. Read the words after "there will be more."
explanation.child: Read Luke 15:7. Find "there will be more." The next word is the answer.
explanation.teen: Check Luke 15:7. Look right after "there will be more."
explanation.older: Luke 15:7 names it directly after the phrase "there will be more."

teaching.extended_explanation: The shepherd called his friends together. In Luke 15:7, Jesus says heaven reacts the same way when one person repents.
teaching.takeaway: There is more joy in heaven over one sinner who repents.

prompt.older: According to Luke 15:15, what work was the younger son sent into the fields to do?

verses.text: Then he went and joined himself to a citizen of that country, and he sent him into his fields to feed swine.

explanation.adult: Luke 15:15 tells what the man sent him to do. Read the end of the verse.
explanation.child: Read Luke 15:15. The end of the verse tells what job he did in the fields.
explanation.teen: Check Luke 15:15. The last words tell what he was sent to do.
explanation.older: Luke 15:15 closes by naming the work he was given at the end of the verse.

teaching.extended_explanation: Luke 15:15 says he was sent to the fields, and Luke 15:16 says he was so hungry he wanted to eat what those animals ate.
teaching.takeaway: The younger son was sent to feed swine.

prompt.adult: When the younger son came home, what did his father do while the son was still far off?

prompt.teen: The son was still a long way off when his father saw him. What did the father do?
prompt.older: According to Luke 15:20, what did the father do when he saw his son still a great way off?

verses.text: “And he arose and came to his father. But when he was still a great way off, his father saw him and had compassion, and ran and fell on his neck and kissed him.

explanation.adult: Luke 15:20 tells what the father did after he saw his son and had compassion. Read the actions that follow.
explanation.child: Read Luke 15:20. The father saw his son and felt compassion. Read what he did next.
explanation.teen: Check Luke 15:20. After the father saw his son, the verse lists what he did.
explanation.older: Luke 15:20 lists the father's actions after he saw his son and had compassion.

teaching.extended_explanation: The son planned to ask to be a servant. Before he even arrived, the father saw him. Luke 15:20 tells what the father did next.
teaching.takeaway: The father ran to his son.

verses.text: But others fell on good ground and yielded a crop

explanation.child: Read Matthew 13:8. Find "others fell." The next words tell where it landed.
